question: What lost-link accidents has the AAIB investigated for the Autel EVO Max 4N?

intake.reason: Identify AAIB investigations related to Autel EVO Max 4N lost-link incidents (record-only, not verified findings)

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance provides claims that losing the control link prompts attempts to reestablish the connection, follow emergency procedures if reestablishment fails, and operate within VLOS or switch to land/hover/return-to-home as needed, with transfers of control only when both pilots maintain VLOS. There is no usable evidence in the approved collection for Autel EVO Max 4N manuals. There is no usable evidence in the approved collection for Autel EVO Max 4N incident reports (unverified accounts). The main gap is that explicit AAIB-lost-link incident details for the Autel EVO Max 4N are missing, leaving uncertainty about outcomes such as RTH success, recovered location, and step-by-step post-loss actions; several open questions remain about automatic signal loss behavior and escalation criteria.

claims.text: When the control link is lost, the guidance says to “Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft.”
claims.quote: Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft.

claims.text: If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.
claims.quote: If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.

claims.text: If the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, the remote PIC or person manipulating the controls should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.
claims.quote: If the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, the remote PIC or person manipulating the controls should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.
conditions: Cannot regain Visual Line of Sight (VLOS)

claims.text: The remote PIC may need to land the small unmanned aircraft immediately, enter hover mode, or employ a return-to-home sequence.
claims.quote: the remote PIC may need to land the small unmanned aircraft immediately, enter hover mode, or employ a return-to-home sequence.
conditions: Loss of VLOS or hazardous situation requiring control action

claims.text: Two or more certificated remote pilots transferring operational control may do so only if they are both capable of maintaining Visual Line of Sight of the small unmanned aircraft without loss of control.
claims.quote: Two or more certificated remote pilots transferring operational control (i.e., the remote PIC designation) to each other may do so only if they are both capable of maintaining Visual Line of Sight (VLOS) of the small unmanned aircraft without loss of control (LOC).
conditions: Both pilots capable of maintaining VLOS without LOC
